16755.head: 1b93d629ae4d189045b17fa4da89445d821aecaf
16755.body_html:
Stacked on #16515; keep draft until dependency lands. Parent head: 14ede099247a63cf3f8084c31257e52b789b383c.

The ambient type-B difference, short, and simple coroot matrices require a commutative ring even though their construction only uses additive operations and one. Generalize all three definitions and the two simple-coroot characteristic equations to AddGroupWithOne. Add public diagonal-form characterization lemmas for difference and short coroots, and use them in the existing bundled coroot proofs.

These child changes affect only TypeB/Root/Generators.lean. The main-relative diff also inherits TypeB/DiagonalCartan.lean from #16515, which generalizes the elementary diagonal API to zero and negation; that prerequisite is unchanged here.

Validation: the changed modules and the CartanBasis and GeneratorRelations callers build. Imported examples work over noncommutative integer-matrix coefficients and infinite indices; both simple-coroot cases normalize through their public API. All 14 scoped environment linters, style, header, namespace, source/import/module guards, and the scoped axiom audit pass. Full-library CI passes on the current commit (run 38646077607).

Roadmap: RepresentationTheory

16656.head: cd0f250bf9d30a2a9ef41c6bbaaaa7ca1b6b501c
16656.body_html:
On a path-connected pointed space (X, x), the DG local systems over C_*(Ω_x X; R) that are isomorphic to the DG local system of a classical local system are exactly those concentrated in degree zero. Together with full faithfulness (#16643), the functor from classical local systems is an equivalence onto them.

New file AlgebraicTopology/DGLocalSystem/Classical/EssImage.lean:

  • essImage_classicalDGLocalSystemFunctor : (classicalDGLocalSystemFunctor R x).essImage = DGRightModuleCat.IsConcentratedInDegreeZero
  • classicalDGLocalSystemEquivalence : LocalCoefficientSystem R X ≌ (IsConcentratedInDegreeZero).FullSubcategory
  • For hM : M.IsConcentratedInDegreeZero, the following. hM.groupAlgebraAction is the action, which factors through loopChainToGroupAlgebra, since chains of positive dimension act by zero for degree reasons and boundaries act by zero by the Leibniz rule. hM.representation is the resulting π₁-representation. hM.classicalDGLocalSystemIso identifies M with the DG local system of LocalCoefficientSystem.ofRepresentation x hM.representation.

New file AlgebraicTopology/LocalCoefficient/Representation.lean:

  • LocalCoefficientSystem.ofRepresentation is the local system of a π₁(X, x)-representation on a path-connected space. It reuses Groupoid.functorOfEndHom and Groupoid.singleObjFunctor with paths chosen from the basepoint, and those paths are the identity at the basepoint (pathFromBase). It has monodromyRepresentation_ofRepresentation. It is @[expose]d so that its fibers are V by definition (characteristic lemmas ofRepresentation_obj and ofRepresentation_map_apply).

Supporting general lemmas:

  • HomologicalComplex.moduleCat_homologyπ_eq_zero_iff: a cycle has zero homology class exactly when it is a boundary.
  • DGRightModuleCat.IsConcentratedInDegreeZero, with mem_grading_iff, differential_eq_zero, op_smul_eq_zero, op_smul_d_eq_zero, of_iso, and an IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms instance.
  • loopHomologyZeroπ_eq_zero_iff, loopZeroChainToGroupAlgebra_eq_zero_iff, loopZeroChainToGroupAlgebra_surjective, loopChainToGroupAlgebra_apply, loopChainToGroupAlgebra_surjective.

This PR is stacked on #16643 (#16632, #15253). Only the last commit is new here.

References: BDHO, Morse homology with DG coefficients, Ch. 2 and 7; Whitehead, Elements of Homotopy Theory, Ch. VI §1.

16613.head: 94cd47a93f533e8edfad30daf11af1f76cc7eb11
16613.body_html:
Stacked on #16611 (merged up): new here are Cubical/LocalCoefficients/Normalized.lean, Cubical/LocalCoefficients/ChainComplex.lean, and (from review) independent universes for the source and target spaces in Cubical/LocalCoefficients/Chains.lean plus a docstring for augment_ofCube.

Roadmap node: DGFloer/README.md, Layer 0, item 3, consequence "cubical local coefficients" (listed under the comparison with simplicial chains: "Consequences, each derived through the comparison and not re-proved: … - cubical local coefficients;"). This is item 1 of intention TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap#878. The normalized complex built here is the object for which the comparison with simplicial chains with local coefficients (twistedChainComplex) will be stated, and it is the prerequisite for that comparison.

This PR adds normalized cubical chains with coefficients in a local system L. The degenerate chains (TwistedCubicalChain.degenerate L n, spanned by the summands of degenerate cubes) form a subcomplex. Take a cube c = s ∘ π that does not depend on its i-th coordinate. Its two i-faces are the same subcube s with the same transported coefficient (ofSubcube_comp), and its other faces are degenerate (boundary_ofCube_mem_degenerate). The normalized chains NormalizedTwistedCubicalChain L n are the quotient by this subcomplex.

Main content:

  • degenerate, ofCube_mem_degenerate, degenerate_le (the induction principle), degenerate_zero, and degenerate_le_comap_{boundary,coefficientMap,map}.
  • NormalizedTwistedCubicalChain.{ofCube, hom_ext, boundary, boundary_ofCube, boundary_boundary, coefficientMap, map, augment}. They come with _mk/_ofCube characteristic lemmas, map_id/map_comp, naturality, and augment_boundary.
  • In ChainComplex.lean: LocalCoefficientSystem.normalizedTwistedCubicalChainComplex L : ChainComplex (ModuleCat R) ℕ with the chain maps normalizedTwistedCubicalChainComplexCoefficientMap η and normalizedTwistedCubicalChainComplexMap f L, plus their id/comp laws and naturality. The complex is @[expose] like the untwisted TauCeti.normalizedCubicalChainComplex, so that X n is definitionally the module of normalized chains. The comparison chain maps with twistedChainComplex are built from linear maps on those chains.

16130.head: c8897d521d6448a721fde38841661cb1e41645a6
16130.body_html:
This PR proves that every rational subset of the closed unit disc is a finite union of holed discs. Let K be an algebraically closed nonarchimedean normed field that is a Tate ring (every algebraically closed field with a nontrivial ultrametric norm is one, by TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing.of_nontriviallyNormedField). Then TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.exists_finset_eq_iUnion_closedSubdisc_inter_iInter_of_mem_spaRationalFamily gives, for every rational subset U of X = Spa(K⟨T⟩, K⟨T⟩°), a finite set P of triples (a, c, H) with

U = ⋃_{(a, c, H) ∈ P} D(a, |c|) ∩ ⋂_{(b, d) ∈ H} {x : x(d) ≤ x(T - b)}.

The statement covers every point of the adic disc, including the rank-two points. Completeness of K is not needed.

Roadmap target: AdicSpaces/README.md, Layer 2, §2.4 "Quotients and classical affinoids": "describe the elementary points and rational subdomains of the closed unit disc (Example 7.57 and the examples following it)". The roadmap status names "the classification of rational subdomains" as a missing part of this milestone, and the descriptions of #16035 "feat: the domain of two coprime polynomials in the closed disc is a finite union of holed discs" and #15928 "feat: holed discs in the closed unit disc" (now merged) name this theorem as the remaining step: "present rational subsets by polynomials (#15856), then intersect the resulting finite unions of holed discs". This PR does that assembly. After this PR, the milestone still needs the five-type exhaustion of the points of the disc, which is #15843 "feat: every point of the closed unit disc is of one of the five types".

The proof:

  • #15856 mem_spaRationalFamily_iff_exists_polynomial presents U as R(G / p) with G a finite set of polynomials containing a unit constant c.
  • If p = 0, U is empty. Otherwise the constant forces x(p) ≠ 0 at every point satisfying the inequalities. So U is the intersection over g ∈ G of the domains {x : x(g / gcd(g, p)) ≤ x(p / gcd(g, p))}, since gcd(g, p) has nonzero value wherever x(p) ≠ 0 and cancels there. In the other direction the constant term itself carries the cancellation, because x(c) ≠ 0. This is the private setOf_forall_vle_eq_iInter_div_gcd. Mathlib's isCoprime_div_gcd_div_gcd makes each pair coprime.
  • #16035 exists_finset_setOf_vle_eq_iUnion_closedSubdisc_inter_iInter describes each domain as a finite union of holed discs. Its private predicate IsHoledDiscUnion gains closure under binary and finite intersections (IsHoledDiscUnion.inter, isHoledDiscUnion_biInter), from its existing closure under intersection with discs and holes.

All changes are in TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/AdicSpace/Spa/Polydisc/PolynomialDomain.lean (+130 lines, 4 changed): the theorem, four private steps, a new section, and an updated module docstring (title, a paragraph on rational subsets, a main-results bullet, and a Bosch–Güntzer–Remmert §7.2 reference). The module now publicly imports Polydisc/RationalSubset.lean (from #15856), and privately imports TauCeti.Topology.Homeomorph.SetCongr for Homeomorph.setCongr_apply. The hypothesis on U uses Homeomorph.setCongr (closedPolydisc_def 1 K), as in holedDisc_mem_spaRationalFamily. The holed discs are written in the same raw form as #16035's theorem, which this proof consumes directly. Restating both theorems with holedDisc, now on main from #15928, would be a separate refactor.

This PR is stacked on #15856 "feat: present rational subsets of the closed disc by polynomials" and #16035, both approved and labelled ready-to-merge. Until they land, the branch carries their commits rebased onto main. The commit specific to this PR is the last one, "feat: every rational subset of the closed unit disc is a finite union of holed discs".

The module cites Wedhorn, Adic Spaces, arXiv:1910.05934v1, Example 7.57; Fresnel–van der Put, Rigid Analytic Geometry and Its Applications, Chapter 2; and Bosch–Güntzer–Remmert, Non-Archimedean Analysis, §7.2. No Mathlib infrastructure or external formalisation is vendored. The cooperative claim registration returned the permitted exit-2 fallback.
